raw_response:
Ai, let me think this through. Three mu ain't much — we got five mouths in the house and my man and the older boy work in town when they can. I do most of the field work with my daughter-in-law helping when she's not busy.

I'll do like I've always done: two mu for the wheat and maize together, one mu on the side for cotton. The wheat-maize gives us our own flour and some corn to sell or feed. Cotton brings in cash when the price is decent, though my back hurts from picking these days.

For the wheat, I'll put it in after the October holiday like everyone in the village. One bag of that fifteen-fifteen-fifteen compound will cover the two mu before we plow — that's what my neighbor老张's wife does and her wheat looks fine. When the wheat greens up in spring I sprinkle some urea, maybe half a bag for the two mu, and water it the same time. I'll water three times if the sky don't give rain — once before the freeze, once at green-up, once when the heads are filling. The well water costs money so I don't waste it. Herbicide once for the weeds, that's all. Seed I buy from the village shop, the kind everyone plants.

Maize goes right in after we cut the wheat — no time to breathe, got to get it in the ground within a few days or it won't make it before the cold. I don't plow, just drill it in. Hybrid seed, the red bag kind. Compound at planting, then urea when it's up to my waist. Water once or twice if it's dry.

Cotton on that one mu by the house — I know that field. Plant late April when the ground is warm. Hybrid seed. Compound before planting, urea when it starts flowering. The bollworm and aphids come every year so I spray two or three times, whatever the shop tells me. Pick it myself with my daughter-in-law, takes many days but we do it together.

I don't buy more fertilizer than I can afford. Better to have a little cash set aside in case someone gets sick than to pour money on the field hoping for more yield.
